text: The selection distance shall be the trail distance plus the braking distance, in feet.

prototype.how: See parent R4.

text: The selection distance is how far ahead the HFDS looks for a lead vehicle. The trail distance is the distance the HFDS keeps behind the lead vehicle. The braking distance is the distance needed to brake from the current speed to a stop. It equals the speed squared, divided by twice. MaxBrakingDecel(in feet) is the largest braking deceleration the HFDS may command.

prototype.how: Braking distance = v^2 / (2 * maxBrakingDecel). Text in SRS is garbled; see ISSUE-03.

text: A vehicle shall be treated as in the lane of the vehicle when any part of its width overlaps the path of the vehicle along the blue path. The width of the vehicle and of the other vehicle decide this overlap, and the length of the other vehicle decides its size class in R6. The weight of the vehicle enters through a_b.

prototype.how: Lateral overlap test between ego path corridor (ego width along blue path) and the other vehicle width. "a_b" in the note is undefined; see ISSUE-04.

text: In the closing zone, the Driver Assist System shall hold the current speed until the gap reaches the coast zone.

prototype.how: Closing zone: hold current speed. Zone boundaries are not defined in the SRS; see ISSUE-05 / A-05.

text: In the coast zone, the Driver Assist System shall coast to match the lead vehicle speed before the safety zone is reached.

prototype.how: Coast zone: zero throttle, natural decel, until speed matches lead; then follow at trail distance.

text: When the closing speed is too high for the distance but within the braking capability of the system, the Driver Assist System shall brake at the required deceleration a_req.

prototype.how: a_req = closingSpeed^2 / (2 * (gap - safetyCushion)); brake at a_req if <= maxBrakingDecel. Worked example from SRS is a unit test.

text: The required deceleration is the constant braking rate that brings the closing speed to zero before the gap shrinks to the safety zone. The closing speed is how much faster the vehicle travels than the lead vehicle, in feet per second; it is 0 if the lead vehicle is as fast or faster, so no braking is needed. The available braking distance is the gap (the distance from the front of the vehicle to the rear of the lead vehicle) minus the safety zone.

prototype.how: See parent R22.

text: The Driver Assist System shall brake at the required deceleration when it is not greater than maxBrakingDecel.

prototype.how: See parent R22.

text: When the gap is not greater than the safety cushion, the Driver Assist System shall treat a_req as greater than maxBrakingDecel. Example: at 60 mph behind a car, d_trail is 176 ft and the safety cushion is 44 ft. With a gap of 100 ft and a closing speed of 20 mph (29.3 ft/s), a_req is about 7.7 ft/, which is below 11.5 ft/s², so the HFDS brakes. With a closing speed of 30 mph (44 ft/s), a_req is about 17.3 ft/s², which is above 11.5 ft/, so the HFDS issues the reclaim-control warning of R23. Note: the statement in R22.1 assumes that the lead vehicle holds its speed or that there is no lead vehicle. If the lead vehicle brakes, the deceleration actually needed is higher than a_req, and the Forward Collision System (IR22) and the reclaim-control warning (R23) cover that case.

prototype.how: See parent R22.

text: When the required deceleration a_req exceeds maxBrakingDecel, the Driver Assist System shall issue a reclaim-control warning to the driver.

prototype.how: a_req > maxBrakingDecel -> Class A reclaim-control warning (UC19).

text: If the lead vehicle leaves the lane, the Driver Assist System shall resume the set speed.

prototype.how: Lead leaves lane -> resumeSetSpeed() (never above 85 mph, IR27).

text: The Driver Assist System shall compute the trail distance as the speed of the vehicle, multiplied by the time gap, multiplied by the size factor(1.00/car and SUV, 1.25/truck,1.50/bus,2.00/semi-truck) of the lead vehicle, in feet. The speed is the speed of the vehicle in feet per second. The time gap is the larger of the driver-selected following gap and the 2.0 second minimum of IR9.

prototype.how: d_trail = v(ft/s) * max(driverGap, 2.0 s) * sizeFactor(lead).
